churn_resistance.rationale: Data access and configuration are genuinely well-centralized, so an Astro upgrade would touch few files — but 'types at boundaries' is absent (all API data is any), the runtime cache has no expiry strategy, and the client scripts live outside Astro's processed script pipeline.

findings.issue: The entire PokeAPI boundary is untyped: every dynamic route builds 'let data: any' and passes any-typed records into the template, with no shared interfaces for species/pokemon/move/ability/type records.
findings.suggestion: Define resource interfaces in src/lib (e.g. types.js) and have data.js return typed views; the pages' data objects then get a narrow view-model type instead of any.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache never expires or evicts: in a long-lived Node server every response (potentially thousands of full move/ability records) is retained forever and never revalidated, even though the spec treats the API as live data that can change at any moment.
findings.suggestion: Add a maxAge/LRU to fetchJson, or adopt Astro 7's stable route caching (cache: { provider: memoryCache() } + routeRules with maxAge/swr, stable since astro@7.0.0 per the v7 upgrade guide).

findings.issue: Browser interactivity lives in public/js/*.js behind is:inline, which Astro does not bundle, type-check, hash, or dedup, and it is coupled to template markup by string IDs (#filters, #results, #game-select) so a rename breaks it silently.
findings.suggestion: Move the scripts into src/ and use Astro's processed <script src="..."> (bundling, TS, automatic inlining per the client-side-scripts guide), or wrap the bits that need it in small custom elements.

findings.issue: The 'fetch, map to view-model, throw 404 on err.status' pattern is duplicated across all four dynamic routes, including the identical catch blocks.
findings.suggestion: Factor a helper in src/lib/api.js (e.g. loadOrNotFound(fn)) so the 404 policy lives in one place.

findings.issue: Upstream fetches have no timeout or AbortController, so a slow API can stall a page render indefinitely (and each of the 32 concurrent workers stays blocked).
findings.suggestion: Add an AbortController with a modest timeout and surface that as a 5xx, keeping the existing cache-invalidation on failure.

summary: This is a current-generation Astro app: latest framework and adapter versions, documented SSR config, zero deprecated APIs, and a platform-first client layer with two dependencies total. It ages poorly mainly at the data boundary, where everything is typed as any and the runtime cache never expires or evicts in a long-lived server. Client scripts also sit outside Astro's processed pipeline, coupled to markup by string IDs.

apis.replacement: documented, but processed <script src> from src/ gives bundling/TS/dedup and is preferred where the code is first-party
unused: Astro 7's stable route caching could replace part of the hand-rolled Map cache
